title: Chord Progression: I–IV–V–I in C
description: The most common progression in Western music: C (I), F (IV), G (V) and back to C, first in root position and then with smooth close-position inversions over a left-hand bass.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: Bars 1-4 use root-position triads over single bass notes; bars 5-8 keep the thumb on or near C and change only the upper fingers (C-E-G, C-F-A, B-D-G), then speed up to quarter notes.
teachingPoints: Bars 1-4: name each chord aloud (I, IV, V, I) as you play it; LH plays the roots C3, F3 and G3 with fingers 5, 2 and 1.
Bars 5-6: the IV chord becomes C-F-A (second inversion) and V becomes B-D-G (first inversion) so the hand barely moves - practise the RH alone until the changes are silent.
Bar 7: one chord per beat - the bass note and the chord must change together.
Final bar: LH open fifth C3-G3 (5-1) under the C triad; let it ring.
